title: Deprecation orchestration: guided rollforward, compatibility shims, and staged notice flow
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem statement: We need a repeatable, low-friction deprecation workflow for old model versions that reduces customer outages and support load, preserves production latency/cost characteristics, and gives clear migration paths. Current gaps: sparse automated notices, no standard compatibility shim, inconsistent SDK warnings, and limited telemetry that ties regressions to specific deprecation stages. This ticket defines a pragmatic orchestration pattern we can implement across hosted, dedicated, and private customers: (1) early advisory + performance profile snapshot, (2) soft-warning in SDKs and console, (3) automated rollforward recommenders and compatibility shims for minor API/response changes, (4) staged traffic shadowing and canary deferrals, (5) final sunset with archive/readonly and migration runbook. Deliverables: notice templates, console UI treatment, SDK warning release, backend APIs for pinning+rollforward, compatibility-shim prototype, telemetry events and dashboards, and a customer-facing migration guide. Links: Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ML/PM-20456+Deprecation+Orchestration, Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/7851, Example migration guide draft: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folder/0B-migration-guides
acceptance_criteria: Notice templates for 90/60/30/14/7/0 day windows drafted and available in Confluence
Console UI mockups showing deprecation state and recommended replacement completed and approved by Design
SDKs emit non-blocking warnings at 60/30/7 days with links to migration guide (major languages: python, js, go)
Backend APIs to record pinned versions and rollforward recommendations implemented and integration-tested
Compatibility shim prototype that maps legacy response shapes to new model variant for simple breaking changes (eg. renamed fields) completed and validated against two sample models
Telemetry events emitted for each deprecation lifecycle action and dashboards created (customer-level signal of attempted pin, migration, and regression rate)
Customer migration guide published and linked from deprecation notices
Runbook for escalations and manual pin extensions available to CS/Support
SLOs and rollback triggers defined for staged sunset (shadowing, canary, cutoff)
notes: Trade-offs: full backward-compatibility shim for arbitrary model changes is infeasible; limit shims to structural/field-level adapters and content-preserving normalizations.
We should prioritize hosted API and Dedicated customers first; Private deployments will get the notice + runbook but require packaged tooling for on-prem installs.
Consider a short-lived 'compat-mode' header that clients opt into; this can be used to route to compatibility runtime that applies light transforms.
Telemetry must include a fingerprint of the model perf profile snapshot (hash) so we can compare pre/post quality and latency regressions tied to a deprecation.
Legal/Compliance: check disclosure requirements for GDPR customers before sending automated notices; coordinate with Legal on language.
